title: I Used the Driving-Range Bucket Clock on the Coach Who Fed His Own Basket

parts.text: I paid bucket 12 at 4:08 p.m. and coach Hale was already feeding a private basket from the hopper. The kiosk said: PAY THE BUCKET. NO STAFF BASKETS. END ON EMPTY. I was thirty-six, member, holding a token receipt. Hale shrugged. "Coaches are the range." I photographed the kiosk, the receipt, and his basket on my hopper. Then I asked for the bucket log. At 4:14 the pro shop pinged why Hale's name was on a private feed. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The pro shop can see Hale's private basket on hopper 12 during my paid bucket.

social.video_title: The coach fed his own basket from my paid hopper — Part 1/2
social.description: Driving range, a token receipt, a staff basket. I logged the feed. Would you have asked the pro shop?

parts.text: Hale called it a demo until the shop asked for the still. I printed the log, the kiosk, and the receipt. The basket stopped. Hale bought tokens and told the next coach demos were always about optics. Optics is a word coaches use when hoppers exist. Clock policy now has a second line: COACHES PAY THE BUCKET. I keep 12. Hale brown-bags the jokes. The range finally looks like a receipt, not a pantry. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Bucket log, stopped basket, and a second line. Was a demo ever my tokens?
